description: Ability to operate, validate, and intervene in AI-automated data preparation and synthesis pipelines, including tuning parameters, monitoring outputs, and handling exceptions.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.'
change to work: Instead of manually executing these data preparation activities for needs identification, the analyst will supervise, interact with, and validate AI-powered data pipelines as they extract, cleanse, transform, and synthesize stakeholder data. Focus moves to monitoring outputs, escalating exceptions, and tuning digital routines.
justification: Transition from manual data manipulation to operating, validating, and troubleshooting automated/AI-powered pipelines requires new technical proficiency.

description: Knowledge of how automated systems work, their biases, typical errors, and strategies for human-led validation and critical review.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.'
change to work: Instead of manually executing these data preparation activities for needs identification, the analyst will supervise, interact with, and validate AI-powered data pipelines as they extract, cleanse, transform, and synthesize stakeholder data. Focus moves to monitoring outputs, escalating exceptions, and tuning digital routines.
justification: Understanding how AI/automation translates stakeholder needs into structured data will demand knowledge of algorithmic limitations, bias, and quality assurance.

description: Ability to manage digital work files, metadata, and system outputs efficiently, including quality control of automated logs and documentation.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies. Maintains work files.'
change to work: Analyst’s role shifts from direct manual collation to ensuring automated outputs are properly organized, consolidated, versioned, and stored—focusing on reviewing for completeness and correcting AI/system-generated gaps.
justification: File and information management becomes more about digital supervision, metadata control, and managing automated logs/version histories.

description: Advanced skillset in understanding, explaining, and critiquing AI-generated outputs, including communicating uncertainty, error, and rationale to non-technical users.
historic work: Technical Activities: 'Data literacy skills are needed to derive meaningful information from data, including the knowledge needed to read, analyze, interpret, visualize and communicate data, as well as understand the use of data in decision-making. Data literacy includes data stewardship and the ability to assess the quality of data, protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use.'
change to work: The domain of data literacy expands to include automated/AI data literacy—understanding both the strengths and caveats of machine-generated insights, limitations, and how to communicate/interpret outputs in partnership with AI.
justification: Need for applied skills in interpreting, validating, and communicating AI-generated data insights—not simply classic analysis.

description: Knowledge of data governance frameworks and ethical practices as applied to AI-driven automation, including privacy, consent, traceability, and liability concerns.
historic work: Skills: 'Provides advice, information and guidance to data users and clients regarding governance concepts used to protect and optimize the utility of Statistics Canada’s data assets.'
change to work: Role expands to offering advice on AI/digital governance—how automation affects data stewardship, ethical concerns, and best practices for working with automated needs specification.
justification: Requires familiarity with new governance frameworks for AI-driven and automated data processes.

description: Skill in reviewing, editing, and contextualizing AI-generated analytical reports and visualizations to ensure clarity, neutrality, and appropriateness for diverse audiences.
historic work: Skills: 'Writing skills are necessary to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science.'
change to work: Reporting increasingly involves explaining, interpreting, and critiquing AI-generated recommendations and business case materials, ensuring that machine-generated drafts are clear, impartial, and contextually valid.
justification: Requires skill in reviewing and revising automated report drafts and integrating critical contextual analysis.

description: Ability to validate AI/automation-synthesized stakeholder needs, review automated benchmarking, and troubleshoot flags/exceptions in digital processes.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.'
change to work: Manual techniques for extracting or cleansing stakeholder input become oversight and validation of algorithmically-processed needs triggers. Analyst intervenes only when automated benchmarks or aggregations produce ambiguous, novel, or context-sensitive cases.
justification: Shift to AI data aggregation and benchmarking requires technical fluency in automation monitoring and exception handling rather than manual sourcing.

description: Proficiency with digital logging, automated documentation, and metadata validation tools for AI-collected needs information.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies. Maintains work files.'
change to work: Information organization is now performed via digital logs and AI-driven documentation. Analyst ensures completeness and contextual relevance of consolidated needs data and validates automated records.
justification: Requires knowledge of digital information management, version control, and automated aggregation documentation systems.

description: Skill in assessing completeness, accuracy, bias, and context in AI-driven stakeholder needs datasets.
historic work: Technical Activities: 'Data literacy skills are needed to derive meaningful information from data...including the ability to assess the quality of data.'
change to work: Quality assessment expands to algorithmically-assembled stakeholder needs, demanding advanced skills in evaluating bias, completeness, and significance of machine-generated data.
justification: Data literacy must now encompass skills in evaluating, critiquing, and confirming quality of automated aggregations.

description: Knowledge of digital/AI tools for automated assessment of source quality/timeliness, including ability to identify, critique, and supplement technical outputs.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.'
change to work: Analyst is now prioritizing technical validation—confirming that AI/digital checks of source quality, coverage, timeliness, and compliance are robust and trustworthy. Expected to spot gaps or weaknesses in automated assessments, especially as new administrative and external sources grow in prominence.
justification: Automation- and AI-first data quality validation requires knowledge of how digital routines assess coverage, timeliness, and origin, and ability to intervene when outputs are non-standard.

description: Skill in supporting, validating, and documenting the automated acquisition, negotiation, and certification of external/alternative data sources—including handling digital agreements, contracts, and compliance metrics.
historic work: Technical Activities: 'Knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis, evolving information sources, survey methodologies, data risk assessment, impact and quantitative analysis in order to assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity.'
change to work: The domain expands to include technical knowledge of administrative and alternative sources, their digital acquisition/validation, and digital risk assessment. Analysts now track, critique, and recommend strategies for automated coordination and negotiation with data suppliers.
justification: Must know best practices for digital acquisition logistics, risk analysis, negotiation documentation, and certification of novel sources.

description: Skill in translating findings from digital/AI data source checks into actionable advice, recommendations, and requests for both internal colleagues and external suppliers.
historic work: Skills: 'As assigned, discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur.'
change to work: Expanded to include technical support for digital sourcing and validation, including outlining gaps between automated/alternative data sources and requirements.
justification: Requires enhanced communication ability to explain digital/AI validation findings, needed improvements, and new supplier requirements.

description: Skill in testing, auditing, and validating AI-generated design documentation, metadata, and system specifications for compliance, interoperability, and analytic readiness.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R, E-Views, SPSS or other similar software.'
change to work: Focus expands to include validation and QA of AI-generated design artifacts and ensuring compatibility/interoperability with analysis environments. Need to collaborate with automated design modules and systems.
justification: Competence in reviewing, testing, and validating outputs from automated design/metadata pipelines and ensuring technical and standards compatibility with downstream analysis tools.

description: Knowledge of automation in statistical design, machine-actionable metadata formats, APIs, and interoperability standards for effective collaboration and configuration in digital-first environments.
historic work: Technical Activities: 'Knowledge of data science and its life cycle...data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence, and exploratory/ confirmatory, predictive analysis...'
change to work: Knowledge must expand to include the automated/AI-powered design and specification tools, standards for machine-actionable metadata, and best practices for digital interoperability.
justification: Understanding of automation, APIs, machine-actionable metadata, and standards as they affect data system design and output configuration.

description: Skill in critically appraising the stewardship, security, provenance, and long-term management of digital/automated design outputs and metadata.
historic work: Technical Activities: 'Data literacy skills are needed to derive meaningful information from data... Data literacy includes data stewardship and the ability to assess the quality of data, protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use.'
change to work: Stewardship responsibility now applies to automated and AI-generated designs; must be able to assess/make recommendations on the quality and digital stewardship of design artifacts and how they will propagate through the lifecycle.
justification: Skill in evaluating provenance, stewardship, and lifecycle management of AI-generated metadata and design outputs.
